skill.name: threejs-fundamentals
skill.description: Three.js scene setup, cameras, renderer, Object3D hierarchy, coordinate systems. Use when setting up 3D scenes, creating cameras, configuring renderers, managing object hierarchies, or working with transforms.

generated_query: I'm creating a 3D visualization of a solar system for an educational website. I need to set up a Three.js scene with a perspective camera that orbits around the sun. The sun should be a glowing sphere at the center, and I want a few planets (different sizes and colors) orbiting around it at different speeds. I also need proper lighting—ambient and a directional light coming from the sun position. The scene should resize automatically when the browser window changes. Can you help me write the complete HTML/JavaScript code for this?

edit_instructions.rationale: Removing the lighting setup leaves the scene dark, failing the user's requirement for ambient and directional light.

Replaces the PerspectiveCamera with OrthographicCamera, which fails the user's explicit requirement for a perspective camera needed for realistic 3D depth perception in the solar system visualization.
Changing to OrthographicCamera removes perspective depth, which is essential for the user's orbiting 3D solar system visualization.
Removing the camera aspect ratio update breaks proper resizing for any camera, making the scene distort on window resize.
The skill's resize handler omits updating the camera's aspect ratio, causing distorted rendering on window resize, which fails the user's requirement for automatic proper resizing.
Replacing the perspective camera with an orthographic camera removes depth perception, making the solar system visualization flat and unrealistic.
Changing the directional light position from near the sun (implied origin) to directly above destroys the intended sunlight direction from the sun center.
Removing the resize handler breaks the auto‑resize requirement, making the scene non‑responsive to window changes.
